issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff is not entitled to exclude the time spent prosecuting an earlier proceeding when the plaintiff fails to establish that the proceeding was pursued with due care and attention and with due diligence.
material_facts: The plaintiff filed a possession suit in a court that lacked pecuniary jurisdiction, and the suit was later returned and re-presented to the proper court after the limitation period had expired.

The plaintiff knew the value of the properties exceeded the original court’s jurisdictional limit but omitted their value from the plaint; he had drafted the plaint himself, while his plaint in a similar suit stated the property’s value.
The plaintiff sought return of the plaint after a similar suit had been dismissed on the merits, although the relevant facts had been known from the outset.
The plaintiff produced no order-sheet or equivalent evidence showing that he had prosecuted the earlier suit with due diligence during its lengthy pendency.
The parties accepted that the earlier proceeding involved the same cause of action and that the earlier court could not entertain it for want of jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff did not establish the requirements for excluding the time spent in the earlier proceeding under section 14, so the suit was barred by limitation. The Court did not decide the separate argument about limitation under Article 142.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(1) of the Limitation Act requires the plaintiff affirmatively to establish that the earlier civil proceeding was pursued with due diligence, was founded on the same cause of action, was prosecuted in good faith, and was in a court unable to entertain it because of a jurisdictional defect or a similar cause. Under section 2(7) of that Act, good faith requires due care and attention; mere honesty is insufficient. The burden initially rests on the plaintiff, and it does not shift to the defendant until the plaintiff satisfies that burden. The Court applied these statutory provisions and cited no earlier cases.

rule.if: civil_suit_seeks_time_exclusion and same_cause_prior_proceeding and prior_court_unable_to_entertain and (prior_prosecution_lacked_due_care or prior_diligence_not_proved)

predicates.civil_suit_seeks_time_exclusion: A plaintiff in a civil suit seeks to exclude time spent pursuing an earlier civil proceeding when calculating limitation.
predicates.same_cause_prior_proceeding: The earlier civil proceeding was founded on the same cause of action as the later suit.
predicates.prior_court_unable_to_entertain: The court handling the earlier proceeding could not entertain it because of a jurisdictional defect or a similar cause.
predicates.prior_prosecution_lacked_due_care: The plaintiff pursued the earlier proceeding without the due care and attention required for good faith, such as by omitting information the plaintiff knew was needed to establish the proper court’s jurisdiction.
predicates.prior_diligence_not_proved: The plaintiff did not provide evidence establishing diligent prosecution of the earlier proceeding.
predicates.time_exclusion_for_prior_proceeding_deni: The time spent pursuing the earlier proceeding is not excluded from the limitation calculation.

issues.definition: When a civil-suit plaintiff seeks time exclusion for an earlier proceeding on the same cause of action that its court could not entertain, the exclusion is denied if the plaintiff pursued it without due care or fails to prove diligent prosecution.
